candidates.review_note: Every cell already has one outgoing edge. All starts return to themselves exactly when the functional graph consists entirely of cycles, equivalently every cell has indegree one. Thus choose a minimum-cost perfect matching between source and destination cells: each of the four wrapped neighbors costs zero for retaining the original direction and one otherwise. If different directions lead to the same neighbor on a narrow grid, take their minimum cost. A uniform direction always provides a feasible perfect matching, so forbidden-edge penalty n+1 exceeds every feasible optimum. Hungarian assignment returns the exact number of modified arrows.
